name: Open Extended Left Colectomy
overview: Open resection extending from mid-transverse to sigmoid

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the extent of bowel removed in an open extended left colectomy?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Distal transverse colon, splenic flexure, descending colon, and sigmoid colon — with ligation of the IMA at its aortic origin and the left branch of the middle colic artery. The anastomosis is between the proximal transverse colon and the upper rectum.

pimpingQuestions.question: What anatomic structures are at risk during the lateral mobilization of the left colon?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Left ureter (at the pelvic brim), left gonadal vessels, left kidney (during splenic flexure mobilization), spleen (splenocolic ligament), and the tail of the pancreas (near the splenocolic/splenorenal attachments).

pimpingQuestions.question: What determines the blood supply to the transverse colon-rectal anastomosis?
pimpingQuestions.answer: The right branch of the middle colic artery and the right gastroepiploic arcade supply the proximal transverse colon. The rectal stump is supplied by the superior rectal artery (if IMA is taken below the left colic) or the middle/inferior rectal arteries (if IMA is taken at its origin).

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the primary challenge of the transverse colon reaching the pelvis?
pimpingQuestions.answer: The transverse mesocolon may be too short, requiring full mobilization of the hepatic flexure and potentially the ascending colon to gain length. Tension at the anastomosis is the primary cause of leak in extended left colectomy.

pimpingQuestions.question: When would you convert an extended left colectomy to a subtotal colectomy?
pimpingQuestions.answer: When the proximal transverse colon cannot reach the pelvis without tension, when synchronous proximal pathology is found, or when the proximal colon is ischemic from collateral interruption.
